questions.question: What happens if you try to instantiate an Abstract Base Class (ABC) directly?
options: It creates the object but with None values
It automatically creates a default child class
questions.explanation: Abstract Base Classes cannot be instantiated directly. Python raises a TypeError because they are designed only to be inherited from, not used directly.

questions.question: What happens if a child class inherits from an ABC but fails to implement one of its abstract methods?
options: The child class will still work, but the method will raise an error when called
The child class will also become abstract and cannot be instantiated
Python will automatically provide a default implementation
The program will crash at import time
questions.explanation: If a child class doesn't implement all abstract methods from its parent ABC, it also becomes an abstract class and cannot be instantiated. Python will raise a TypeError when you try to create an instance.

questions.question: What is the correct way to import what's needed for abstract classes?
questions.explanation: Import `ABC` (the base class) and `abstractmethod` (the decorator) from the `abc` module. Your abstract class inherits from `ABC`, and abstract methods use `@abstractmethod`.
